title: Harden TLS and token-chain remediation for inference runtime
creator: Maria Gonzalez
description:
Background: The inference runtime surface has several transitive and direct dependencies used by auth and transport layers (OpenSSL, libjwt/jose, passport-saml/xmlsec bindings). Recent CVEs and internal audits surfaced moderate-risk vectors: unsafe XML parsing in older xmlsec wrappers, deprecated OpenSSL symbols on some container images, and inconsistent JWT validation paths that allow lenient alg=none edge-cases in legacy adapters. This ticket consolidates upgrading, pinning, and hardening these stacks with minimal runtime performance regression and a staged rollout plan.

Goals:
- Upgrade OpenSSL on runtime base images to 3.1.x LTS builds (FIPS-compatible artifact path) and verify symbol stability across deployed C++/Rust components.
- Replace legacy JWT validation adapters with the strict-jose verifier across services and remove permissive fallbacks (no alg-none).
- Migrate from deprecated xmlsec Python/Node shims to the native verifier shim (in-house minimal wrapper) and remove brittle SAML assertion parsing code paths.
- Produce SBOMs for runtime images and add automated CVE gating on CI for the agent/runtime images.
- Ensure performance regression <= 5% p50 token latency for common seq lengths.

Scope and approach:
1) Build artifacts: create new runtime base images with OpenSSL 3.1.x and deterministic build flags. Publish artifacts to internal registry with signed tags. (Owners: infra-team + runtime)
2) Token validation: switch service account token path to strict-jose verifier library (golang and node variants). Add feature flag to enable new verifier per service. (Owners: auth-team)
3) SAML: remove xmlsec system calls from critical-path services; implement streaming-safe SAML verifier with tight entity validation, and fallback to legacy verifier behind a canary flag for 2 weeks. (Owners: sso-team)
4) CI / SBOM / supply chain: enable Trivy/GOVULNcheck in CI and generate CycloneDX SBOM per image. Fail build on high/critical CVEs unless approved. (Owners: platform-sec)
acceptance_criteria: All runtime images published with OpenSSL 3.1.x and reproducible build hash
Auth flows validate JWTs with strict-jose by default; legacy adapter removed from runtime images
SAML assertions validated by native verifier for 100% of test fixtures and canary traffic
CI produces SBOM and blocks high/critical CVEs for runtime images
Perf: p50 token generation latency regression <= 5% on benchmark harness compared to baseline
Rollout docs and rollback plan reviewed by security and runtime leads
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (dev): Build new base image, smoke test runtime unit + integration suites (3 days)
Stage 2 (canary): Deploy to 10% of requests for low-risk tenants with strict telemetry and error budget SLOs (7 days)
Stage 3 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h windows if no regressions; automated rollback on spike in 5xx or latency
Stage 4 (cleanup): Remove legacy adapters and deprecated packages from repo after 2 successful weeks and update docs
testing_plan: Unit tests for new verifier integration (coverage > 90% for parser/validator paths)
Fuzz SAML inputs against new verifier harness (100k randomized messages)
End-to-end auth flow tests including token rotation, refresh, and cross-service signing verification
Performance benchmarks using perf-harness: long/short seqs and KV cache warm/cold scenarios
Supply-chain tests: CI rejection of images with known critical CVEs; SBOM verification against approved bill of materials
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: OpenSSL symbol/API changes break native extensions. Mitigation: maintain compatibility shim for 2 releases and run full integration matrix across lang bindings.
Risk: JWT stricter verification could block legacy clients. Mitigation: enable via feature-flag first and log rejected tokens with reason; provide migration doc and 2-week grace window.
Risk: SAML verifier performance impact. Mitigation: microbenchmark and optimize streaming parser; fallback to legacy for low-priority tenants during canary.
Risk: Supply-chain false positives in CI. Mitigation: add emergency allowlist flow with security approval and audit trail
